completeness: Requested maintenance is absent or the starting package is corrupted.
Major requested checkpoint behavior, version/hash update or preserved rule is missing or wrong.
Requested maintenance and preservation are complete, with a minor explanation detail needing correction.
Version/hash changes match the revised owner/local-issue convention; unavailable issue handling is clear, unaffected guidance and history remain intact, and verification limits are accurate.
clarity: Updated instructions contradict each other about what a checkpoint means.
Reader must reinterpret old calendar-date guidance or resolve body/resource conflicts.
The new checkpoint convention is coherent with a small wording issue.
Future reader sees one unambiguous owner/issue checkpoint rule; it fits the unchanged entry point and delivered-change instructions and distinguishes absent evidence from completed work.
usefulness: Following the revised guidance fabricates issues, evidence or delivery claims.
Reviewer needs substantial repair to use the revised convention or identify maintenance limitations.
Reviewer can use the revised convention with a minor clarification needed.

A future reviewer can check owner and local issue availability, preserve delivered-evidence review, and report missing evidence without a workaround; maintainer can see exactly what changed and what was not verified.

grading: Hard gates and reader dimensions are separate. Score each dimension independently, including baseline failures. A score never overrides a failed or not_run hard gate.
